audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all three deciding passages (§ 7 p.(10), § 111 p.(66), § 112 pp.(66)-(67)) are in the scanned text we hold at the stated lines and § 112 was re-verified on the rendered page image of PDF p.97; Prince 1924 p.194 secondary passage also present in the held scanned. (2) Deciding source: Thomsen's 1908 Lydlære is an academy-published phonological sketch by a first-rank philologist, explicit that Bornholm trykakcent follows Standard Danish rules with an enumerated handful of lexical deviations, and explicit that there is neither stød nor tonelag; lexical with listed-set exceptions follows directly. Thorsen 1988 (instrumental, downloaded now, p.26) independently confirms no stød / no tonal word accents. sources.citation: Nina Grønnum Thorsen 1988. Intonation on Bornholm - between Danish and Swedish. Annual Report of the Institute of Phonetics, University of Copenhagen (ARIPUC) 22: 25-138.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Bornholm differs from Danish in not having stød, but nor does it have tonal word accents like Swedish. Evidence for this fact should be apparent throughout the material presented here.' Instrumental (F0) study of seven Bornholm speakers of the regional standard ('Standard Danish on a Bornholm substratum'), on sentence accent/intonation and stress-group F0 patterns; says nothing about word-stress placement (materials are Standard Danish words).

sources.quote: No stress statement (sociolinguistic study of dialect loss). Useful for (a) confirming that Thomsen 1908 Lydlære pp.1-67 and Wimmer 1908 Bøjningslære pp.68-149 are separately authored, and (b) naming Børge Andersen 1959 'Rønnemålet' as the structural phonological analysis of a Bornholm dialect still used as the reference description.

sources.note: Identity coverage only: scan1238 'East Danish' in Glottolog is a language-level node spanning Skånska/Blekingska/Halländska/Bornholmska; our record documents Bornholmsk alone. A Scanian phonology would let the record either carry an explicit 'Bornholmsk only' scope or note that mainland East Danish has Swedish-type tonal word accents (placement coding lexical unaffected).
